query: Silences in Jars {Today the headmistress hands you an empty jar. "Seal a silence in it. Not quiet; silence. You will know the difference by the end."|Another empty jar. Behind the headmistress, a shelf of stoppered jars, all apparently empty, all labelled in faded hands.|Silence jars. You know the weight of a well-sealed one now, heavier than it looks.} {The lamp hisses.|The books on the shelves have stopped breathing, as if to help.|{final_year: She asks what silence you'd keep, if you could keep only one.|She works at her own jar, unhurried, while you work at yours.}} Seal the room's silence {You draw the room's silence into the jar a breath at a time and stopper it. When you shake it, nothing happens, very heavily. She nods.|The silence fights the stopper like a cat fights a bath. You win, eventually, emptied out.|You seal a silence so clean that the lamp seems louder when you're done. The headmistress takes the jar and shelves it with the old ones.} Unseal one of the old jars {You unstopper a jar dated a century ago. Out comes the silence of a room just after someone laughed. It's unbearably sad, and you don't know why.|You open an old jar and the room fills with the silence of a held breath before a goodbye. You close it again quickly. She says nothing, kindly.|You open one more old jar. A silence after snow. You sit in it a long while before you can speak.}
